blocks.text: Śiva Is Literally Doing a One-Man Show, and You’re Every Character.
blocks.directed: Śiva Is Literally Doing a One-Man Show, and You’re Every Character.

blocks.text: Now, given everything we’ve just learned, consider what this means.
blocks.directed: Now, given everything we’ve just learned, consider what this means.

blocks.text: The universe is the manifestation of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The universe is the manifestation of consciousness.

blocks.text: The apparent objects are its radiance.
blocks.directed: The apparent objects are its radiance.

blocks.text: The individual is consciousness experienced under conditions of contraction.
blocks.directed: The individual is consciousness experienced under conditions of contraction.

blocks.text: And so what is the relationship between Śiva and the manifest universe?
blocks.directed: And so what is the relationship between Śiva and the manifest universe?

blocks.text: And here’s the really extraordinary part.
blocks.directed: And here’s the really extraordinary part.

blocks.text: The dancer doesn’t simply stand outside the performance controlling it from a distance.
blocks.directed: The dancer doesn’t simply stand outside the performance controlling it from a distance.

blocks.text: The dance is the dancer’s own activity.
blocks.directed: The dance is the dancer’s own activity.

blocks.text: The movement is not an independently existing substance.
blocks.directed: The movement is not an independently existing substance.

blocks.text: It’s the dancer expressing their power.
blocks.directed: It’s the dancer expressing their power.

blocks.text: And this is precisely the kind of relationship Trika describes between Śiva and Śakti.
blocks.directed: And this is precisely the kind of relationship Trika describes between Śiva and Śakti.

blocks.text: Śiva is not an inert observer watching Śakti do all the work.
blocks.directed: Śiva is not an inert observer watching Śakti do all the work.

blocks.text: Śiva’s very nature is inseparable from the freedom of his power.
blocks.directed: Śiva’s very nature is inseparable from the freedom of his power.

blocks.text: The luminosity of consciousness and its reflexive self-awareness.
blocks.directed: The luminosity of consciousness and its reflexive self-awareness.

blocks.text: The manifestation of reality is not foreign to this unity.
blocks.directed: The manifestation of reality is not foreign to this unity.

blocks.text: Now imagine an actor on a stage.
blocks.directed: Now imagine an actor on a stage.

blocks.text: And an extraordinarily complicated political situation.
blocks.directed: And an extraordinarily complicated political situation.

blocks.text: And for the duration of the drama, an entire world becomes manifest through the performance.
blocks.directed: And for the duration of the drama, an entire world becomes manifest through the performance.

blocks.text: But the actor is not ultimately identical with the limited role.
blocks.directed: But the actor is not ultimately identical with the limited role.

blocks.text: And now Vasugupta takes this analogy and applies it to consciousness.
blocks.directed: And now Vasugupta takes this analogy and applies it to consciousness.

blocks.text: The apparent absence of differentiated experience in deep sleep.
blocks.directed: The apparent absence of differentiated experience in deep sleep.

blocks.text: These are different modes of the cosmic performance.
blocks.directed: These are different modes of the cosmic performance.

blocks.text: And the Self is the dancer moving through them.
blocks.directed: And the Self is the dancer moving through them.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explicitly explains the sūtra through the manifestation of different roles across the states of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explicitly explains the sūtra through the manifestation of different roles across the states of consciousness.

blocks.text: The yogi recognises the underlying Self as the actor displaying these changing conditions through its own powers.
blocks.directed: The yogi recognises the underlying Self as the actor displaying these changing conditions through its own powers.

blocks.text: He supports the interpretation with references to the Naiśvāsatantra, Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa’s Stavacintāmaṇi and the Īśvarapratyabhijñā. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He supports the interpretation with references to the Naiśvāsatantra, Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa’s Stavacintāmaṇi and the Īśvarapratyabhijñā. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, the actor becomes identified with the role.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, the actor becomes identified with the role.

blocks.text: “These are the terrible things that happened to me.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “These are the terrible things that happened to me.”

blocks.text: And the role becomes the apparent totality of existence.
blocks.directed: And the role becomes the apparent totality of existence.

blocks.text: Imagine an actor who becomes so absorbed in playing Hamlet that he forgets he’s an actor.
blocks.directed: Imagine an actor who becomes so absorbed in playing Hamlet that he forgets he’s an actor.

blocks.text: He wanders around after the performance convinced that Denmark is in crisis.
blocks.directed: He wanders around after the performance convinced that Denmark is in crisis.

blocks.text: Somebody tries to offer him a sandwich.
blocks.directed: Somebody tries to offer him a sandwich.
[short pause] “BEGONE, WRETCH, THE KINGDOM IS LOST.”

blocks.text: The performance finished twenty minutes ago.
blocks.directed: The performance finished twenty minutes ago.

blocks.text: That’s an imperfect but helpful analogy for the structure of contraction.
blocks.directed: That’s an imperfect but helpful analogy for the structure of contraction.

blocks.text: The actor becomes absorbed in a particular form of its own manifestation.
blocks.directed: The actor becomes absorbed in a particular form of its own manifestation.

blocks.text: Recognition is the disclosure of the actor’s deeper nature.
blocks.directed: Recognition is the disclosure of the actor’s deeper nature.

blocks.text: But there is something even more subtle here.
blocks.directed: But there is something even more subtle here.

blocks.text: Because in an ordinary theatre, the actor and the audience are separate people.
blocks.directed: Because in an ordinary theatre, the actor and the audience are separate people.

blocks.text: The stage is an independent physical structure.
blocks.directed: The stage is an independent physical structure.

blocks.text: The script has been written by somebody else.
blocks.directed: The script has been written by somebody else.

blocks.text: And the actor is constrained by circumstances that exist independently of him.
blocks.directed: And the actor is constrained by circumstances that exist independently of him.

blocks.text: But in the Trika metaphysical vision, the supreme reality is the source of the entire performance.
blocks.directed: But in the Trika metaphysical vision, the supreme reality is the source of the entire performance.

blocks.text: The powers through which it is experienced.
blocks.directed: The powers through which it is experienced.

blocks.text: All belong to the same consciousness.
blocks.directed: All belong to the same consciousness.

blocks.text: And that means the cosmic theatre is not merely an analogy for pretending.
blocks.directed: And that means the cosmic theatre is not merely an analogy for pretending.

blocks.text: It’s an analogy for manifestation through freedom.
blocks.directed: It’s an analogy for manifestation through freedom.

blocks.text: The performance is real as manifestation.
blocks.directed: The performance is real as manifestation.

blocks.text: But its deepest reality is not separate from its source.
blocks.directed: But its deepest reality is not separate from its source.

blocks.text: And the actor is none other than Śiva.
blocks.directed: And the actor is none other than Śiva.

blocks.text: “The Self is a spectator sitting motionless while the universe dances.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “The Self is a spectator sitting motionless while the universe dances.”

blocks.text: And this is what makes the Trika understanding of consciousness so distinctive.
blocks.directed: And this is what makes the Trika understanding of consciousness so distinctive.

blocks.text: The divine is not merely pure existence stripped of all activity.
blocks.directed: The divine is not merely pure existence stripped of all activity.

blocks.text: Not necessarily frivolous amusement, but spontaneous divine expression.
blocks.directed: Not necessarily frivolous amusement, but spontaneous divine expression.

blocks.text: And the realised yogi recognises the relationship between the changing performance and the conscious actor.
blocks.directed: And the realised yogi recognises the relationship between the changing performance and the conscious actor.

blocks.text: Which means that ordinary life doesn’t have to be rejected as spiritually meaningless.
blocks.directed: Which means that ordinary life doesn’t have to be rejected as spiritually meaningless.

blocks.text: The actor can still play the role.
blocks.directed: The actor can still play the role.

blocks.text: But now the role is understood through its source.
blocks.directed: But now the role is understood through its source.

blocks.text: Instead of identifying entirely as the individual agent moving through a separate world, the yogi recognises the activity as a manifestation of conscious power.
blocks.directed: Instead of identifying entirely as the individual agent moving through a separate world, the yogi recognises the activity as a manifestation of conscious power.

blocks.text: And now, naturally, we need a stage.
blocks.directed: And now, naturally, we need a stage.

blocks.text: Because even Śiva can’t put on a production without somewhere to stand.
blocks.directed: Because even Śiva can’t put on a production without somewhere to stand.

blocks.text: Apparently the cosmic theatre has a technical rider.
blocks.directed: Apparently the cosmic theatre has a technical rider.
